title: Winners and Losers from Hungarian GP F1 Practice
paragraphs: The Hungarian Grand Prix practice sessions highlighted key performances, with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton topping the sessions, while Mercedes struggled, with George Russell finishing fifth. Aston Martin faced challenges with Lance Stroll's suspension failure but showed potential with Fernando Alonso's performance. Lando Norris emerged as a strong contender, and Alpine struggled without upgrades, leaving them at the back of the midfield.

title: Antonelli Penalised for Yellow Flag Violation in Hungary Qualifying
paragraphs: Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, has received a three-place grid penalty for failing to slow sufficiently during yellow flags in Q3 of the Hungarian Grand Prix. Despite lifting off the throttle after Max Verstappen's spin, stewards determined his speed reduction was 'less than 1%'. Antonelli qualified fourth but will start seventh due to the penalty.
The stewards noted that while Antonelli did reduce his speed, it was deemed insufficient. He also received one penalty point on his superlicence, bringing his total to four in the last 12 months.

title: Aston Martin's Major Upgrade Stuns Rivals at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Aston Martin's significant upgrade to its AMR26 car has impressed rivals at the Hungarian Grand Prix, with Fernando Alonso advancing past Q1 for the first time this season. Competitors like Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas and Williams' Alex Albon expressed concern and admiration for Aston Martin's performance leap, which is rumored to be a two-second gain. Alonso noted that while the upgrade has shown promise, there is still potential to unlock in the car.

title: F1 2026 Hungarian GP Starting Grid After Hamilton, Antonelli Penalties
paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton was initially the fastest in qualifying for the Hungarian Grand Prix but faced a setback in Q3. He received a three-place penalty for obstructing Oscar Piastri. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli also received a three-place penalty for not slowing down for yellow flags during Q3. The starting grid has been adjusted accordingly.

title: F1 Monitors Hungaroring Track Surface After Driver Complaints
paragraphs: The FIA is monitoring the Hungaroring track surface after drivers reported issues with bumps and deterioration. Concerns were raised during a drivers' briefing, leading to a track inspection. While some repairs were made, the surface remains inconsistent, affecting grip and potentially increasing tyre degradation. Drivers, including George Russell and Oscar Piastri, expressed dissatisfaction with the track conditions, particularly at the final corner.

title: Hamilton Penalized, Loses Front Row Start at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton has received a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri during Q3 of the Hungarian Grand Prix, dropping him to fifth on the grid. Hamilton, who was initially fastest in Q3, expressed confusion over Ferrari's strategy that led to a chaotic final lap, allowing Lando Norris to secure pole position.

The stewards ruled that Piastri was 'unnecessarily impeded' by Hamilton, who was unaware of Piastri's approaching lap. Additionally, championship leader Kimi Antonelli was penalized three places for failing to slow for yellow flags during the session.

title: Hamilton Prepares for Damage Limitation After Grid Penalty in Hungary
paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton is gearing up for a race of 'damage limitation' after receiving a three-place grid penalty following Qualifying for the Hungarian Grand Prix. Hamilton qualified second but was found guilty of impeding Oscar Piastri, resulting in a drop to fifth on the grid.

In his post-Qualifying interview, Hamilton expressed disappointment at missing out on pole position and acknowledged the challenges ahead, stating, 'Tomorrow’s probably going to be damage limitation.' He congratulated Lando Norris on his performance and reflected on the session's difficulties.

title: Hungarian Grand Prix 2026 F1 Qualifying Results
paragraphs: Lando Norris secured pole position in qualifying for the Hungarian Grand Prix with a time of 1m17.207s. He was closely followed by Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, who finished second and third respectively. The top ten also included drivers from McLaren, Mercedes, Red Bull, and Audi.

title: Norris Claims Pole Position at Hungarian GP Qualifying
paragraphs: Lando Norris secured pole position for the Hungarian Grand Prix, edging out Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012 seconds. Hamilton initially led after the first runs but was penalized three grid places for impeding Oscar Piastri, starting him fifth. Charles Leclerc qualified third, while Max Verstappen spun during his final attempt, finishing sixth.

title: Norris Claims Pole in Thrilling Hungarian Qualifying
paragraphs: Lando Norris secured pole position for the Hungarian Grand Prix after a dramatic qualifying session, narrowly beating Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012 seconds. Hamilton, who initially held provisional pole, received a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri, who will start fifth. Norris expressed confidence in his team's performance and acknowledged the challenge posed by Ferrari in the race.

Piastri, who showed promising pace throughout the session, was frustrated after his final lap was compromised by Hamilton. Both drivers and their team emphasized the progress made with new upgrades, while Hamilton remained hopeful of recovering positions during the race despite his penalty.

title: Norris Tops Final Practice at 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Lando Norris of McLaren secured the top spot in the final practice session for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix, outpacing Lewis Hamilton by 0.117 seconds. This ended Ferrari's dominance in the earlier sessions, with Kimi Antonelli from Mercedes close behind in third.

The session saw Red Bull drivers struggling, with Max Verstappen finishing seventh. Meanwhile, Racing Bulls and Audi battled for midfield positions, with Liam Lawson narrowly ahead of Nico Hulkenberg for ninth.

title: Tactical Options for the Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: At the Hungaroring, track position is often thought to be crucial, but historical data suggests otherwise. Since 2020, no driver has won from pole position, and only three drivers have achieved this in the last ten years.

title: Verstappen Critiques Red Bull's Degradation During Qualifying
paragraphs: Max Verstappen expressed frustration over car degradation during Hungarian Grand Prix qualifying, stating his RB22 became 'completely undriveable' by Q3. He noted that the car's aerodynamic issues worsened throughout the session, leading to a spin on his final attempt. Teammate Isack Hadjar also faced difficulties, finishing eighth and echoing concerns about a lack of progress this weekend.

title: What to Watch for in the Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Lando Norris and McLaren are facing a challenging season as defending champions, having yet to secure a victory this year. Fans will be keen to see if they can turn their fortunes around at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

title: Winners and Losers from F1 2026 Hungarian GP Qualifying
paragraphs: The 2026 Hungarian GP qualifying saw Lando Norris claim his first pole position of the season, while Aston Martin made significant strides with Fernando Alonso reaching Q2 for the first time this year. Mercedes faced challenges, with both drivers struggling for pace and Hamilton receiving a grid penalty. Max Verstappen also had a disappointing session, citing issues with his car's performance.

title: 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix Grid Positions Announced
paragraphs: Lando Norris will start from pole position for the first time as reigning champion at the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix, with Charles Leclerc alongside him on the front row. Lewis Hamilton, who qualified second, drops to fifth due to a three-place grid penalty.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli also faces a three-place demotion, starting seventh. Sergio Perez will begin the race from the pit lane after set-up changes to his Cadillac during Parc Ferme conditions.

title: Alonso Optimistic After Aston Martin's Upgraded Car at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Fernando Alonso expressed optimism following Aston Martin's first race with their upgraded car at the Hungarian Grand Prix, hoping for a 'new start of the championship' in the season's second half. Alonso reached Q3 for the first time this season, while Lance Stroll achieved his best result in P13, with Alonso finishing P14.

Alonso noted the car's competitiveness, especially in the early stages of the race, and highlighted the need for further improvements, particularly in straight-line speed, as the team looks forward to upcoming updates at the Dutch Grand Prix.

title: Antonelli Extends Championship Lead with P3 Finish in Hungary
paragraphs: Kimi Antonelli secured a podium finish in the challenging Hungarian Grand Prix, increasing his lead in the Drivers' Championship. Despite starting P4 and facing a grid drop to P7 due to a yellow flag infringement, Antonelli's strategic decisions allowed him to climb back to P3, finishing ahead of Lewis Hamilton, who received a time penalty.

Antonelli expressed satisfaction with the result, emphasizing the importance of damage limitation for Mercedes. With a break before the season resumes, he leads the standings by 50 points over Ferrari, while teammate George Russell finished P7 after an early setback.

title: F1 Drivers Concerned Over 'Lottery' Track Surface at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Drivers at the Hungarian Grand Prix have expressed concerns over a 'lottery' track surface, particularly a significant bump at Turn 1. George Russell criticized the resurfacing quality, while Lando Norris noted the difficulty in achieving consistent grip. Carlos Sainz and others echoed these sentiments, highlighting the poor conditions and the need for further analysis of the resurfacing work done compared to previous years.

title: Hamilton Regrets Mistakes After P5 Finish at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton expressed frustration after finishing P5 at the Hungarian Grand Prix, following a series of setbacks. Despite qualifying P2, a three-place grid penalty for impeding another driver hindered his race. Hamilton's strategy included starting on soft tyres, but he faced challenges, including a five-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane.

Charles Leclerc also struggled, finishing P4 after starting on the front row. Both drivers acknowledged missed opportunities for Ferrari, with Leclerc noting the need to analyze grip expectations from the car settings.

title: Honda's New F1 Engine Set for Debut at Hungarian Filming Day
paragraphs: Honda's new Formula 1 engine for Aston Martin will debut during a filming day in Hungary next week. This follows a set of chassis upgrades that allowed Fernando Alonso to qualify 16th, while both he and Lance Stroll finished 13th and 14th in the race. Honda's Shintaro Orihara emphasized the importance of the new engine for future progress.

Aston Martin's Mike Krack noted the team's improved pace in Hungary, stating their objective was to return to competitive racing. Alonso highlighted the collaboration between Aston Martin and Honda, acknowledging the need for both sides to address their weaknesses as they aim for further improvements.

title: Hulkenberg Mixed on Qualifying Performance at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Nico Hulkenberg qualified P10 for the Hungarian Grand Prix, expressing mixed feelings about the larger gap to his rivals despite a trouble-free session. His time of 1m 18.686s was slightly slower than his Q2 effort, leaving him cautious about the deficit to P9 and P8. Hulkenberg remains optimistic about competing with midfield teams during the race.

title: McLaren Triumphs at Hungarian GP as Russell Struggles and Ferrari Falters
paragraphs: The 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix saw McLaren's Lando Norris secure his first win of the season, showcasing impressive pace throughout the weekend. Red Bull's Max Verstappen finished second after a challenging race, while Kimi Antonelli climbed to third despite a grid penalty. George Russell faced difficulties, finishing seventh, and Ferrari's promising start faded as Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton ended up fourth and fifth, respectively.

title: Mercedes Evaluates Russell's Cracked Engine Ahead of Grid Penalty
paragraphs: Mercedes is assessing whether George Russell's damaged engine from the Hungarian Grand Prix can be repaired to avoid a grid penalty after the summer break. Russell suffered a cracked sump, leading to a water leak that affected his rear tyres during Q3.

The team has already replaced the power unit, which was only recently fitted, but this marks the fourth engine Russell can use before facing penalties. A detailed analysis of the damaged engine will determine if it can be repaired, impacting both drivers' standings in the title race.

title: Noel Leon Wins F2 Feature Race in Budapest, Camara Closes Points Gap
paragraphs: Noel Leon secured his first FIA Formula 2 Feature Race victory in Budapest, starting from third on the grid. He took the lead after a well-timed pit stop during a Virtual Safety Car period, holding off Rafael Camara and Kush Maini in the closing stages.

Maini finished second, marking his return to the podium, while Camara's third-place finish allowed him to narrow the points gap in the championship standings. Nikola Tsolov remains the points leader despite a recovery from a grid penalty.

title: Norris Claims First Win of 2026 at Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Lando Norris secured his first Grand Prix victory of the year in Budapest, overcoming teammate Oscar Piastri after a strategic race. Piastri initially took the lead but faced issues with traffic and a gearbox failure, allowing Norris to take the win. Red Bull's Max Verstappen finished second, managing to navigate race challenges and capitalize on strategic decisions.

title: Norris Claims First Win of 2026 in Dramatic Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Lando Norris secured his first Grand Prix victory of 2026 at the Hungarian GP, finishing ahead of Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli. The race featured mid-race drama, including a retirement for Norris' teammate Oscar Piastri due to a gearbox issue, which led to a Virtual Safety Car. Despite a strong challenge from Lewis Hamilton, who received a penalty, Norris maintained his lead to clinch the win.

title: Norris Claims First Win of F1 Title Defence at Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Lando Norris secured his first victory of the Formula 1 season at the Hungarian Grand Prix, marking a successful title defence for McLaren. After a tense race, Norris overcame early frustrations with teammate Oscar Piastri, who led until a gearbox failure forced him to retire with 14 laps remaining.

Max Verstappen capitalized on a virtual safety car to finish second for Red Bull, while Kimi Antonelli's strategic two-stop strategy earned him third. Lewis Hamilton and George Russell faced challenges, with Hamilton finishing fifth and Russell recovering to seventh after a poor start.

title: Norris Claims Victory at 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Lando Norris secured his first victory of the 2026 Formula 1 season at the Hungarian Grand Prix, successfully defending his title. The race concluded after 70 laps, with Norris finishing ahead of Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli, who took second and third respectively, despite a five-second penalty for Lewis Hamilton.

title: Norris Claims Victory at Hungarian Grand Prix with Impressive Pace
paragraphs: Lando Norris celebrated his first Grand Prix win of the season at the Hungarian Grand Prix, delivering what he described as 'some of the best pace I’ve ever had.' After initially losing the lead to teammate Oscar Piastri, Norris regained control following a strategic pit stop and maintained a strong performance to finish ahead of Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli.

Reflecting on his race, Norris expressed confidence in the car's performance and the team's efforts, noting the significant upgrades that contributed to their success. He aims to carry this momentum into the upcoming Dutch Grand Prix.

title: Piastri Reflects on Retirement After Backmarker Incident in Hungary
paragraphs: Oscar Piastri expressed disappointment after a challenging Hungarian Grand Prix, where he went from leading the race to retiring due to a collision with Carlos Sainz's Williams. Piastri started third, took the lead early, but faced difficulties after his second pit stop, ultimately suffering a gearbox failure. He acknowledged the unexpected nature of the incident and emphasized the need to reset and improve during the summer break.

title: Piastri and Sainz Clash Sparks Controversy at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Oscar Piastri expressed anger towards Carlos Sainz after a collision during the Hungarian Grand Prix, attributing it to Sainz's 'unacceptable' driving. Sainz defended himself, citing a malfunctioning blue flag system that hindered communication about being lapped. The incident led to a five-second penalty for Sainz, which was reduced due to mitigating circumstances. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff criticized the handling of backmarkers, calling for better communication from teams.

title: Slater Claims F3 Victory and Championship Lead in Budapest
paragraphs: Freddie Slater secured his first Formula 3 victory in Budapest, overtaking Ugo Ugochukwu to take the championship lead. Slater, starting from P2, now leads Ugochukwu by eight points as they head into the summer break. Ugochukwu finished second after a strong drive from sixth, while Brando Badoer took third.
The race concluded the Budapest round of FIA Formula 3, with drivers set to return for a two-day test in Madrid on August 24-25, ahead of Round 8 in Monza from September 4-6.

title: Stella Cautious on McLaren's Hungary Pole Position Significance
paragraphs: McLaren's Team Principal Andrea Stella acknowledges Lando Norris's pole position at the Hungarian Grand Prix but remains cautious about its implications. He believes Ferrari still holds an advantage, particularly in corner grip, despite McLaren's recent upgrades. Stella emphasizes that while the upgrades improved performance, the pole may be an over-achievement due to optimal execution in challenging conditions.

title: Verstappen's Resilient Drive Earns Driver of the Day in Hungary
paragraphs: Max Verstappen showcased his determination at the Hungarian Grand Prix, finishing second after starting from fourth on the grid. Despite not having the fastest car, he successfully held off both Ferraris and Mercedes, finishing behind Lando Norris.
Verstappen received 18.9% of the fan vote for Driver of the Day, narrowly beating Norris, who garnered 17.1%. Kimi Antonelli, George Russell, and Oscar Piastri also received notable votes.

title: Winners and Losers from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Lando Norris claimed victory at the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix, showcasing impressive pace throughout the race. Max Verstappen finished second, benefiting from a strategic tire choice by Red Bull, while Kimi Antonelli secured third place, extending his championship lead. Conversely, Oscar Piastri faced a disappointing DNF after a promising start, and Ferrari's performance fell short, finishing fourth and fifth despite expectations for a stronger showing.

title: Aston Martin Shows Progress at Hungarian Grand Prix After Upgrades
paragraphs: The Hungarian Grand Prix marked a significant weekend for Aston Martin, showcasing improvements from their revised chassis package. The team managed to outpace Cadillac, Williams, and Haas during the race, a notable achievement after a challenging season. Chief Trackside Officer Mike Krack emphasized the importance of reliability and performance development, as both drivers finished in P13 and P14 despite some setbacks, including a suspension failure for Lance Stroll.

title: Edd Straw's 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix F1 Driver Rankings
paragraphs: The 2026 Formula 1 season's first half concluded with the Hungarian Grand Prix, showcasing a surprising driver ranking order by Edd Straw. The rankings reflect driver performance over the weekend, considering factors like pace, racecraft, and consistency. Notably, Lando Norris topped the list, while Pierre Gasly and Nico Hulkenberg also performed well despite their car limitations.

title: Ferrari's Missed Opportunity at Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur expressed frustration over the team's performance at the Hungarian Grand Prix, citing 'poor' execution and 'too many mistakes' as key issues. Despite outscoring Mercedes by one point, Vasseur noted that much more was expected from the SF-26, especially after a strong showing in practice. Drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton both faced challenges, with Leclerc highlighting the car's inconsistency and Hamilton reflecting on strategic missteps.

title: Hamilton's Penalty Woes Continue at Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton has expressed the need to avoid giving the FIA stewards reasons for penalties after receiving his fourth sanction in three races at the Hungarian Grand Prix. He was penalized for speeding in the pitlane, dropping him from fourth to fifth place. Hamilton acknowledged his mistakes and emphasized the importance of not putting himself in situations that lead to penalties.

Team principal Fred Vasseur noted that Hamilton's speeding violation was marginal, suggesting it stemmed from a series of errors during the pit stop. Hamilton's recent penalties include a jump start at Silverstone and a collision in Belgium, but he does not believe there is a campaign against him.

title: Hulkenberg Reflects on First Points for Audi in Hungary
paragraphs: Nico Hulkenberg expressed relief after scoring his first points for Audi in the Hungarian Grand Prix, finishing P9. He utilized a two-stop strategy to overtake competitors in the closing laps, marking a significant achievement for the team in their debut F1 season. Audi now sits eighth in the Constructors' Championship, having scored points in three consecutive races.
Teammate Gabriel Bortoleto, who finished just outside the points in P11, praised the team's progress and acknowledged the challenges faced during the race, particularly with tire strategy.

title: Hungarian Grand Prix Highlights: Drama, Proposals, and Legacy Moments
paragraphs: The Hungarian Grand Prix delivered an exciting race with Lando Norris claiming victory, while Max Verstappen finished second and Kimi Antonelli extended his title lead. Notable moments included a couple's engagement in the Haas garage and the renaming of Turn 2 to 'Hamilton' in honor of Lewis Hamilton's legacy at the track.

Additionally, Czech President Petr Pavel attended as an official photographer, and Mercedes celebrated their team spirit with a dinner. The weekend also featured a special Mercedes Safety Car and Alex Albon's unique helmet design for his 100th race with Williams.

title: Key Takeaways from the Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: The Hungarian Grand Prix revealed significant challenges for top F1 teams, with Ferrari missing a podium despite strong potential. George Russell faced ongoing struggles, while Red Bull's Max Verstappen dealt with aerodynamic issues. Aston Martin's new 'B-spec' chassis impressed, raising concerns among midfield competitors. The team is also anticipating a Honda upgrade to address straight-line speed deficiencies.

title: Lawson Outshines Lindblad in Hungarian Grand Prix Strategy Battle
paragraphs: In the Hungarian Grand Prix, Racing Bulls drivers Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad showcased a strategic battle, with Lawson ultimately gaining the upper hand. Despite Lindblad qualifying ahead, Lawson's two-stop strategy allowed him to finish P8, while Lindblad dropped to P10 after a one-stop plan faltered. Both drivers contributed to Racing Bulls' strong performance, moving the team to P5 in the World Championship.

title: Mekies Credits Red Bull Strategy for Verstappen's P2 Finish in Hungary
paragraphs: Max Verstappen secured a second-place finish in the Hungarian Grand Prix, aided by strategic calls from Red Bull. Team boss Laurent Mekies praised the pit wall for their quick decisions during the race, particularly during a late Virtual Safety Car period. Despite struggles with car balance throughout the weekend, Verstappen's performance and the team's strategy allowed them to achieve a strong result.

Mekies acknowledged that while Red Bull faced challenges, including complaints from both Verstappen and teammate Isack Hadjar, the team executed well, finishing P2 and P6. He noted that improvements are needed to enhance the car's performance as they head into the summer break, with Verstappen's home race in Zandvoort next.

title: Norris Claims Pole in Upgraded McLaren at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Lando Norris achieved his first pole position of 2026 at the Hungarian Grand Prix, showcasing the significant upgrades made to his McLaren car. This marks a notable achievement for both Norris and the McLaren team at the Hungaroring.

title: Norris Secures McLaren Victory at Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Lando Norris achieved his first Grand Prix win of the year at the Hungarian Grand Prix, leading McLaren back to victory. He faced competition from his teammate before pulling away to secure the win, with Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli completing the podium. Antonelli's third place allowed him to extend his lead in the standings, despite challenges faced by Mercedes and other drivers during the race.

title: Russell's Start Issues at Hungarian GP Not Due to Battery Pack Problem
paragraphs: George Russell faced a challenging start at the Hungarian Grand Prix, hitting anti-stall and briefly falling to the back of the field. Initial theories suggested a battery pack issue, but Mercedes later confirmed the problem stemmed from rev control management, leading to insufficient power for a proper launch.

Russell expressed frustration over the situation, emphasizing the team's commitment to understanding and resolving the issues. The longer start sequence in Hungary may have contributed to the complications experienced during the race.

title: Stella Praises Respectful Racing Between McLaren Drivers in Hungary
paragraphs: Andrea Stella commended the respectful racing between McLaren drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri during the Hungarian Grand Prix, where Norris secured his first win of the season. Despite Piastri's early lead, he faced challenges, including a collision with a back marker, leading to his retirement. Stella noted that both drivers exhibited fair competition and expressed satisfaction with their performance and the team's strategy.

title: Vasseur Criticizes Ferrari's Performance at Hungarian Grand Prix
paragraphs: Fred Vasseur expressed disappointment with Ferrari's performance at the Hungarian Grand Prix, stating that 'everything went wrong' as both Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton failed to reach the podium. Despite strong expectations following Friday practice, Leclerc finished fifth and Hamilton ended up in P5 after a series of mistakes and penalties.

Vasseur highlighted the need for improvement in execution and engine performance, acknowledging that while Ferrari has closed the gap to Mercedes, upgrades alone are insufficient. He emphasized the importance of maintaining development momentum as the season progresses.

title: Wolff Reflects on Tough Weekend for Mercedes at Hungarian GP
paragraphs: Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff expressed disappointment after a challenging Hungarian Grand Prix weekend, where the team struggled to keep pace with rivals. Kimi Antonelli secured a podium finish in third, while George Russell recovered to seventh despite a difficult start caused by car issues. Wolff noted that missing FP1 and setup problems hindered their performance, leading to a feeling that they could have achieved more.

title: Ferrari's begun trial of Mercedes F1 qualifying trick
paragraphs: Ferrari has begun testing Mercedes' Formula 1 qualifying lift-off trick in a bid to help boost its challenge for pole positions. As first revealed by The Race , Mercedes has found a clever way to get around F1's ramp down rates to unleash maximum energy deployment across the timing line on qualifying laps. The team is playing catch-up as pushing to the end of last year to ensure it won both the drivers’ and constructors’ championship put it on the back foot. It is due to complement a major car upgrade package introduced by Aston Martin at last weekend’s Budapest round, with the AMR26 absorbing no fewer than 16 developments . paragraphs: Three drivers and teams have stayed on at the Hungaroring to take part in a Pirelli tyre test, with the programme focused on development of the 2027 compounds.
